SEBI Young Professional Program 2026 Vacancy Details

The total number of vacancies for SEBI Young Professional Program Recruitment 2026 is 91 posts distributed among domains as under:

Domain Number of Young Professionals
Young Professional (Securities Market Operations) 40
Young Professional (Law) 13
Young Professional (Research) 4
Young Professional (Information Technology) 29
Young Professional (Rajbasha) 5
Total 91

The Board reserves the right to modify the number of Young Professionals to be engaged or not to engage any Young Professional at all.

Eligibility Criteria

1. Age & Nationality

  • The candidate must be an Indian citizen.
  • Age must not be more than 30 years as on the date of publication of the advertisement.

2. General Essential Skills (for all domains)

All candidates are expected to have reasonable:

  • Understanding of financial markets.
  • Analytical ability.
  • Knowledge of Information Technology tools.
  • Aptitude for research.
  • Oral and written communication skills.
  • Judgment and interpersonal skills.

3. Domain-wise Educational Qualification, Work Experience & Skills

Young Professional (Securities Market Operations)

  • Post Graduate qualification (degree / 2-year diploma) in Management (with specialization in Finance) from a recognized and reputed university/institution with minimum 60% aggregate marks or equivalent CGPA; OR
  • Chartered Accountant (CA) / Company Secretary (CS) / Cost Management Accountant (CMA) with minimum 55% aggregate marks in the final level of the course; OR
  • Successfully completed all 3 levels of Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) course from CFA Institute (USA).
  • At least 1 year of work experience in the financial sector after completion of Post Graduate qualification or CA/CS/CMA/CFA.

Young Professional (Law)

  • Bachelors’ Degree in Law from a recognized and reputed university/institution with minimum 60% aggregate marks or equivalent CGPA.
  • At least 1 year of work experience in corporate/securities laws after completion of Bachelors’ Degree in Law / LLM.
  • Preference to candidates with experience in a financial or investment environment requiring knowledge of market practices and rules, regulations and guidelines governing the securities industry.

Young Professional (Research)

  • Post Graduate qualification (degree / 2-year diploma) in Management (with specialization in Finance) / Economics / Commerce / Financial Economics / Business Economics / Applied Statistics / Econometrics from a recognized and reputed university/institution with minimum 60% aggregate marks or equivalent CGPA.
  • For candidates with only Post Graduate qualification: at least 1 year of research/work experience in areas including but not limited to financial markets, corporate finance, macroeconomic theory, corporate governance, financial institutions and related areas of international finance, supported by published work/working papers/submission of papers in research conferences.
  • For candidates with PhD in relevant fields (Economics/Econometrics/Finance/Commerce, preferably focused on financial markets): work experience requirement is not mandatory.
  • Skill: Knowledge of statistical software.

Young Professional (Information Technology)

  • Any of the following degrees from a recognized and reputed university/institution with minimum 60% aggregate marks or equivalent CGPA:
    • B.E. / B.Tech in Electronics / Electronics and Communication / Information Technology / Computer Science; OR
    • MCA / MSc (IT) / MSc (Computer Science) / MBA (Systems) / MBA (Analytics) / M.Tech (Computer Science/IT/Relevant Stream) / MS (Computer Science/IT/Relevant Stream) or equivalent degree.
  • At least 1 year of work experience in software development (programming) or cyber security.

Skills – Software Development (Programming)

  • Proficiency in any of: JSP/J2EE with Spring/Hibernate; Angular; SAP-ABAP/Web Dynpro; Python (with ML frameworks like Pandas, Pytorch, scikit-learn, NumPy, Matplotlib, Plotly); IBM BPM development.
  • Knowledge of ML algorithms, Deep Learning frameworks and NLP; or deep understanding of statistical concepts and methodologies including Multivariate Analysis, anomaly and pattern detection techniques, graph database.
  • Proficiency in front-end frameworks like React, Vue etc. and/or knowledge of digital forensic analysis or OSINT frameworks.
  • Database proficiency in DB2/ORACLE/PostgreSQL/MySQL etc.

Skills – Cyber Security

  • Knowledge of global best practices in cyber security and IT.
  • Ability to take corrective measures/prudent response in case of cyber-attacks.
  • Experience in development, implementation and compliance with cyber and information security policies and procedures.
  • Installation/operation of Data Security (DLP/DAM), Network Security (Firewall/IPS/Proxy/DDoS), or System Security (PIM/Antivirus/Anti-APT) products.

Young Professional (Rajbasha)

  • Master’s Degree in Hindi/Hindi Translation with English as a subject at Bachelor’s Degree level; OR
  • Master’s Degree in Sanskrit/English/Economics/Commerce with Hindi as a subject at Bachelor’s Degree level; OR
  • Master’s Degree in both English and Hindi/Hindi Translation from a recognized University/Institute.
  • At least 1 year of work experience in the field including knowledge of Hindi typing.

Age Limit

  • Maximum age: Not more than 30 years as on the date of publication of advertisement.

Selection Process for SEBI Young Professional Program 2026

Candidates will be selected based on a three-step process:

  • 1. Application Screening: Applications will be screened and shortlisted as per criteria decided by SEBI, which may include institute ranking (e.g. NIRF), academic performance, relevance of work experience, Statement of Purpose, extracurricular activities, and overall profile.
  • 2. Preliminary Interview: Conducted in virtual mode for shortlisted candidates.
  • 3. Final Interview: Conducted in virtual mode; candidates must have valid ID proof for verification as required.

For Young Professionals (IT), additional factors considered may include relevant programming/cyber security certifications, valid GATE score and achievements in coding competitions, bug bounty, hackathons, or zero-day vulnerability reporting.

SEBI’s decision regarding eligibility, screening, interviews, assessment, number of vacancies and results will be final and binding. SEBI may select or reject any candidate and may cancel the advertisement fully or partly.

How To Apply

Eligible candidates can apply online for SEBI Young Professional Program 2026 by following these steps:

  1. Visit SEBI’s official website: www.sebi.gov.in and go to the “Careers” section.
  2. Access the Young Professional Program online application form at:
    Apply for SEBI YPP 2026.
  3. Fill the online application form carefully with accurate personal, academic, experience and domain choice details. A candidate is permitted to apply for only one domain.

Vacancy Details

Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation (MRVC), a Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Railways, is recruiting 7 professionals for Rolling Stock projects on a 5-year contractual basis. These positions are critical for executing EMU (Electric Multiple Unit) projects and enhancing suburban rail transportation capacity in Mumbai.

Position Vacancies Category Pay Scale (IDA)
Sr. Manager (Rolling Stock) 3 UR E4 (₹70,000 - ₹2,00,000)
Manager (Rolling Stock) Included in 3 UR E3 (₹60,000 - ₹1,80,000)
Project Engineer (Rolling Stock) 4 3 UR, 1 OBC E1 (₹40,000 - ₹1,40,000)

Eligibility Criteria

Educational Qualification

  • B.E / B.Tech in Electrical, Mechanical, Electrical & Electronics, Power Electronics, or Instrumentation from a Government recognized University/Institute
  • Minimum 60% marks in engineering graduation (aggregate percentage as per university conversion norms if CGPA/OGPA/CPI/DGPA is awarded)
  • Note: Rounding off percentages will NOT be acceptable (e.g., 59.99% will be treated as less than 60%)

Experience Requirements (Post-Qualification)

  • Sr. Manager (Rolling Stock): Minimum 8 years post-qualification working experience. Currently working in E-3/L-10 grade with minimum 2 years in that level or higher grade
  • Manager (Rolling Stock): Minimum 4 years post-qualification working experience. Currently working in E-2/L-8 grade with minimum 2 years in that level or higher grade
  • Project Engineer (Rolling Stock): Minimum 2 years post-qualification working experience
  • Preferred: Candidates with working experience in design, technical specifications, bid preparation, testing, operation and maintenance of EMU rolling stock in Railway/RRTS/Metro/LRT/HSR/Suburban rail systems will be preferred

Age Limit (as on 28.02.2026)

  • Sr. Manager (Rolling Stock): Not exceeding 40 years
  • Manager (Rolling Stock): Not exceeding 35 years
  • Project Engineer (Rolling Stock): Not exceeding 30 years
  • Age relaxation as per Government of India policy applicable

Important Dates

Event Date
Notification Released 29.01.2026
Last Date for Application Submission 28.02.2026
Eligibility Cut-off Date 28.02.2026
Document Verification & Interview To be announced (5x vacancies will be shortlisted)
Contract Period 5 Years

Selection Process

  • Preliminary Screening: Applications will be screened for compliance with eligibility criteria and prescribed format
  • Shortlisting: If more applications are received, candidates equal to 5 times the notified vacancies will be shortlisted based on engineering marks and experience
  • Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates must bring original application, original certificates, one set of self-attested photocopies, and character certificate from Gazetted/Executive Officer
  • Interview: Candidates will be interviewed by a nominated Committee of MRVC
  • Merit-Based Selection: Final selection will be based on performance in interview, qualifications, and post-qualification experience
  • Medical Examination: Selected candidates must pass medical fitness examination by a doctor (minimum MBBS qualification)
  • Decision: The decision of the Nominated Committee shall be final and binding

Salary/Remuneration

  • Sr. Manager (Rolling Stock) - IDA E4/L-11: Basic Pay ₹70,000 - ₹2,00,000 with annual increment @ 3% of basic pay
  • Manager (Rolling Stock) - IDA E3/L-10: Basic Pay ₹60,000 - ₹1,80,000 with annual increment @ 3% of basic pay
  • Project Engineer (Rolling Stock) - IDA E1: Basic Pay ₹40,000 - ₹1,40,000 with annual increment @ 3% of basic pay
  • Additional Allowances: DA (Dearness Allowance), HRA (House Rent Allowance), Provident Fund, Cafeteria, and other perks as per MRVC policy
  • Medical Benefits: As per MRVC policy
  • Pay Protection: Provided to candidates already working in Govt/Semi-government/PSU organizations (including on contract)

How to Apply

Application Process

  1. Download the application proforma (Annexure-I) from the official PDF
  2. Fill the application form completely with all required information in the prescribed format
  3. Paste a recent passport-size photograph and sign across it
  4. Fill all mandatory fields including:
    • Full name, father's/husband's name, postal address with PIN code
    • Contact details (mobile number and email address)
    • Date of birth in DD/MM/YYYY format
    • Gender, Category (SC/ST/OBC/UR)
    • Current working position and pay level
    • Complete educational qualifications with aggregate percentage marks
    • Detailed work experience in chronological order

Required Documents (Self-Attested)

Mandatory Documents:

  • Copy of original application with photo and signature
  • Certificates in proof of educational qualifications (all degrees/diplomas)
  • Proof of Date of Birth (SSLC/SSC Certificate or Birth Certificate)
  • OBC-NCL certificate in format prescribed for Central Government employment (if applicable)
  • Photo ID proof (Aadhar Card or PAN Card)
  • Documents regarding work experience and last service record
  • Character certificate from Gazetted Officer or Executive Officer
  • NOC from Government/PSU employer if currently employed

Recommended Documents:

  • Employment letters from previous and present employers
  • Form 16 (Income Tax) from previous/present employer
  • EPF/PF Number documentation

Submission Mode

  1. Email the duly filled application with all supporting documents to: [email protected]
  2. Subject line format: "Application for [Position Name] - [Your Name]"
  3. Application must be received by 28.02.2026 (email timestamp will be considered)
  4. Incomplete applications or those without prescribed documents will be summarily rejected
  5. No correspondence will be entertained regarding rejection

  • Assistant Librarian: A Master's Degree in Library Science, Information Science or Documentation Science or an equivalent professional degree, with at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade in a point-scale, wherever the grading system is followed). A consistently good academic record, with knowledge of computerization of a library. Besides fulfilling the above qualifications, the candidate must have cleared the National Eligibility Test (NET) conducted by the UGC, CSIR or similar test accredited by the UGC like SLET/SET or who are or have been awarded a Ph.D. Degree in accordance with the University Grants Commission Regulations, 2009 or 2016 and their amendments from time to time

Essential Qualifications

  • Educational qualification, experience, age of retirement on superannuation and pay scales of Professor, Associate Professor, Assistant Professor, Deputy Librarian and Assistant Librarian will be as per the UGC/NCERT, Government of India norms as amended from time to time and in force at the time of closing date of filling-up online application
  • For Assistant Professor and Assistant Librarian positions, NET/SLET/SET shall not be required for such Masters Programmes in disciplines for which NET/SLET/SET is not conducted by the UGC, CSIR or similar test accredited by the UGC
  • Candidates registered for the Ph.D. programme prior to July 11, 2009, shall be governed by the provisions of the then existing Ordinances/Bye-laws/Regulations of the Institution awarding the degree and such Ph.D. candidates shall be exempted from the requirement of NET/SLET/SET subject to fulfillment of specific conditions: Ph.D. degree awarded in regular mode, Ph.D. thesis evaluated by at least two external examiners, Open Ph.D. viva voce conducted, Candidate has published two research papers from Ph.D. work (at least one in refereed journal), Candidate has presented at least two papers based on Ph.D work in conferences/seminars sponsored/funded/supported by the UGC/ICSSR/CSIR or any similar agency
  • The fulfillment of these conditions is to be certified by the Registrar or the Dean (Academic Affairs) of the University concerned
  • The Academic score as specified in Appendix II for Universities and Colleges shall be considered for short-listing of the candidates for interview only, and the selections shall be based only on the performance in the interview as per UGC Regulations-2018 and as amended from time to time

Experience

  • Professor: A minimum of ten years of teaching experience in university/college as Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor, and/or research experience at equivalent level at the University/National Level Institutions with evidence of having successfully guided doctoral candidate OR ten years experience as an outstanding professional from academic institutions/industry with significant contribution to the knowledge in the concerned discipline
  • Associate Professor: A minimum of eight years of experience of teaching and/or research in an academic/research position equivalent to that of Assistant Professor in a University, College or Accredited Research Institution/industry
  • Deputy Librarian: Eight years experience as an Assistant University Librarian/College Librarian with evidence of innovative library services including integration of ICT in library
  • Assistant Professor and Assistant Librarian: No specific years of experience required, but must have NET/SLET/SET qualification or Ph.D. degree exemption as per UGC norms

Desirable

  • For Professor positions: Published work of high quality, actively engaged in research with evidence of published work with a minimum of 10 research publications in the peer-reviewed or UGC-listed journals and a total research score of 120
  • For Associate Professor positions: A minimum of seven publications in the peer-reviewed or UGC-listed journals and a total research score of 75
  • For Deputy Librarian: Evidence of innovative library services including integration of ICT in library
  • For Assistant Librarian: A consistently good academic record with knowledge of computerization of a library

Salary/Stipend

  • Professor: Academic level 14 with rationalized entry pay of Rs. 1,44,200/- per month (Pre-revised scale of pay: Rs.37,400-67,000 with AGP-10,000)
  • Associate Professor/Deputy Librarian: Academic level 13A with rationalized entry pay of Rs. 1,31,400/- per month (Pre-revised scale of pay: Rs.37,400-67,000 with AGP-9,000)
  • Assistant Professor/Assistant Librarian: Academic level 10 with rationalized entry pay of Rs. 57,700/- per month (Pre-revised scale of pay: Rs.15,600-39,100 with AGP-6,000)
  • All pay scales are as per UGC/NCERT/Government of India norms and will be applicable as amended from time to time
  • Selected candidates will be entitled to other allowances and benefits as per Government of India/NCERT rules applicable from time to time

Age Limit (as on 20/02/2026)

  • Age of retirement on superannuation will be as per the UGC/NCERT, Government of India norms as amended from time to time and in force at the time of closing date of filling-up online application
  • The relaxation in age and percentage of marks to candidates belonging to SC/ST/OBC(NCL)/EWS/PWD categories is provided in accordance with the UGC/GOI/NCERT rules
  • Persons with Disability (PWD) having disability less than forty percent will not be considered. The disability certificate shall be from a competent medical board constituted by the central or state Government Hospital
  • Such persons should meet the prescribed criteria of physical disability of the respective category as per the Government of India rules

Application Fee

  • UR/OBC/EWS Candidates: Rs. 1000/- (Rupees One thousand only) through online payment mode only
  • Women applicants and applicants belonging to SC/ST/PWD: Exempted from payment of fee
  • No other mode of payment will be accepted other than online payment mode
  • Fee once paid shall not be refunded under any circumstances

Advertisement Number 177/2026

Extended Last Date of Online Registration and apply online 06/03/2026 (Up to 05:00 PM)

Selection Process

  • For Assistant Professor Posts: Up to 50 candidates (category-wise) for the first vacancy and 05 candidates for every additional vacancy will be called for the interview in order of their rank/merit in the list as prepared by the Shortlisting Committee on the basis of marks scored by the candidates, which should not be less than academic score of 60 (Sixty) in any case. In case of tie of marks at the 50th place for 01 vacancy and tie of marks at 5th place for every additional vacancy, all candidates whose marks tie will be called for interview
  • For Professor and Associate Professor Posts: The existing criterion of minimum academic score as per UGC guidelines will be followed subject to the condition up to 10 candidates (category-wise) for the first vacancy and 05 candidates for every additional vacancy will be called for interview in order of their rank/merit in the list as prepared by the Shortlisting Committee on the basis of marks scored by the candidates. In case of tie of marks at the 10th place for 01 vacancy and tie of marks at 5th place for every additional vacancy, all candidates whose marks tie will be called for interview
  • The Academic score shall be considered for short-listing of the candidates for interview only, and the selections shall be based only on the performance in the interview
  • The list of shortlisted candidates will be displayed on the NCERT website
  • The shortlisted candidates will be allowed to appear for the interview only after verification of their eligibility
  • The registration will be provisional as the eligibility of the shortlisted candidate will be verified at the time of Interview from the original documents
  • All Certificates, Degrees and other documents must be produced in original for verification at the time of interview (if shortlisted), failing which the candidate may not be allowed to appear for the interview
  • Final result of the selected candidates will be displayed on NCERT website
  • The Council will not entertain any correspondence with the candidates about their non-selection in the recruitment
  • The decision of the NCERT in all matters relating to selection and allotment of posts/organizations to selected candidates will be final and binding on the candidates

General Information/Instructions

  • National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) is an apex organization for Educational Research, Teacher Training and Development of Curriculum and Instructional material in school education

  • The Selection methodology will comprise of Computer Based Test (CBT) only. No personal interview will be held.

    • Experience: I. 5 years in Central/State educational institutes/organisations of repute. II. Demonstrated meritorious performance in national/international events (at least twice in past 4 years). III. Representation at University/College/State/National level competitions. IV. Evidence of organising competitions and coaching camps of at least 2 weeks. V. Evidence of having produced good team/athlete performances at State/National/Inter-University level.
  • Junior Translator (Rajbhasha) (Group B, Level 6, UR-01)
    • Upper Age Limit: 35 years.
    • Qualification: Master’s Degree from recognised University in:
      • Hindi with English as compulsory/elective or medium at degree level, OR
      • English with Hindi as compulsory/elective or medium at degree level, OR
      • Any subject with Hindi medium and English as compulsory/elective or medium, OR
      • Any subject with English medium and Hindi as compulsory/elective or medium, OR
      • Any subject with both Hindi and English as compulsory/elective or one as medium and other as compulsory/elective at degree level.
    • Experience: At least 5 years office environment experience with Hindi/English typing skills, excellent computer skills for correspondence/files, and knowledge of translation (Hindi–English and vice versa).

Application Fee

  • Application Fee: Rs. 500 per post (non-refundable) to be paid online.
  • Exempted Categories: Women, SC, ST, Ex-servicemen, PwD and Transgender candidates (on uploading relevant self-attested certificates/ID).
  • Fee once paid will not be refunded under any circumstances.
  • Separate applications and separate fees are required for each post applied.

How To Apply

  • Applications must be submitted online only through IISER Berhampur website: www.iiserbpr.ac.in (online link under recruitment section).
  • No hard copy of application is required to be sent at the time of online submission.
  • During online application, candidates must upload legible self-attested copies (where applicable) of:
    • Educational qualifications and marksheets.
    • Experience certificates.
    • Caste/Community certificate, PwD/Transgender certificate, Ex-servicemen discharge certificate, etc.
    • Valid ID proof issued by State/Central Government.
  • Scan and upload photograph and signature as per specified guidelines:
    • Photo: Recent colour passport size, 200x230 px, 10–100 KB, .jpg/.jpeg, light background.
    • Signature: On white paper with black/blue pen, 140x60 px, 10–100 KB, .jpg/.jpeg; signature in CAPITAL letters not accepted.
  • All communication, including recruitment schedule, shortlist/rejection lists and updates, will be made via email and institute website; candidates must provide an active email ID and check the website regularly.

  • For existing regular IISER Berhampur employees, there is no upper age limit, provided at least one year of service remains before superannuation on last date of application.
  • Deputation posts will follow DoPT guidelines; deputation term generally three years, extendable as per rules.
  • Institute may conduct written and/or trade tests, fix additional shortlisting criteria, and alter number of positions (including consequential vacancies) based on requirements.
  • Mere fulfilment of eligibility does not guarantee being called for test; shortlisting will be as per institute’s criteria and decision will be final; canvassing will lead to disqualification.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Citizenship: A candidate must be a citizen of India.
  • Age Limit: A candidate must have attained the age of 21 years and must not be above the age of 42 years as on 1st January 2025; he/she must not have been born earlier than 2nd January 1983 and not later than 1st January 2004. Upper age limit is relaxable by 5 years for SC/ST/SEBC/Women/Ex-Servicemen and by 10 years for PwD with permanent disability of 40% or more, with cumulative benefit for PwD of SC/ST/SEBC categories.
  • Educational Qualification (Essential): A candidate must hold a Bachelor’s Degree from any University incorporated by an Act of the Central or a State Legislature in India or an Educational Institution established by an Act of Parliament or deemed to be a University under Section-3 of the UGC Act, 1956 or a Foreign University approved by the Central Government from time to time.
  • Odia Language Requirement: The candidate must be able to read, write and speak Odia and must have passed Middle School Examination with Odia as a language subject OR passed High School Certificate or equivalent examination with Odia as medium of examination in non-language subjects OR passed Odia as a language subject in final examination of Class-VII from a recognised school OR passed a test in Odia in Middle English School standard conducted by the Government of Odisha.
  • Marital Status Condition: A candidate who has more than one spouse living or, in case of a woman candidate, is married to a person having one spouse living, shall not be eligible unless exempted by the State Government.
  • Government Servants: Government servants (temporary or permanent) are eligible, provided they possess requisite qualifications and are within the prescribed age limit and obtain No Objection Certificate from the competent authority.
  • Character & Health: A candidate must have good moral character and be of sound mental and physical health and free from any physical defect likely to interfere with the discharge of duties.

Salary/Stipend

  • For Odisha Police Service, Group-A (Junior Branch) – Group-A Service: Rs. 56,100/- in Level-12, Cell-1 in the Pay Matrix under Rule-3 of ORSP Rules, 2017.
  • For Group-B Services (Odisha Taxation & Accounts Service, Odisha Co-operative Service, Odisha Skill Development & Employment Service, Odisha Labour Service, Odisha Excise Service, Odisha Tourism Service): Rs. 44,900/- in Level-10, Cell-1 in the Pay Matrix under Rule-3 of ORSP Rules, 2017.

Age Limit

  • Minimum Age: 21 years.
  • Maximum Age: 42 years.
  • The candidate must not have been born earlier than 02/01/1983 and not later than 01/01/2004.
  • Upper age limit relaxable by 5 years for SC, ST, SEBC, Women and Ex-Servicemen candidates.
  • Upper age limit relaxable by 10 years for Persons with Disabilities having permanent disability of 40% or more; PwD candidates of SC/ST/SEBC categories are eligible for cumulative age relaxation.

Application Fee

  • Candidates other than SC, ST and PwD category shall have to pay examination fee of Rs. 700/- (Rupees Seven hundred only).
  • Payment Mode: Online mode while filling the Online Application Form (Credit Card, Debit Card, UPI, Net Banking, Wallet, etc.).
  • The examination fees paid shall be refunded only to those candidates who actually appear in both the papers of the Preliminary Examination.
  • Applications without payment of examination fee (except SC/ST/PwD candidates) will be treated as incomplete and summarily rejected.
  • Candidates must furnish bank account details in the Online Application Form for refund where required.

Important Dates

Event Date
Issue of Advertisement / Notice 31 December 2025
Start date for registration and payment of examination fee 20 January 2026
Last date for registration and payment of examination fee 20/02/2026 (5.00 P.M.)
Last date for submission of registered online application 27/02/2026 (5.00 P.M.)
Tentative date of Preliminary Examination of OCS-2025 07/06/2026 (Sunday)

Selection Process

  • The Combined Competitive Recruitment Examination shall comprise:
    • Preliminary Examination (Objective type) for selection of candidates for Main Examination.
    • Main Examination (Written) and Interview for Personality Test for selection to various services and posts.
  • Preliminary Examination: Two compulsory papers of Objective Type (Multiple Choice Questions), General Studies Paper-I (200 marks) and General Studies Paper-II (200 marks), each of 2 hours duration.
  • General Studies Paper-II is a qualifying paper with minimum qualifying marks of 33; selection to Main Examination is based on marks in General Studies Paper-I and qualifying the Paper-II as per rules.
  • There shall be negative marking: for each wrong answer, one-third (0.33) of the marks assigned to a question shall be deducted; multiple answers to a question are treated as wrong.
  • Main Examination: Written examination consists of nine papers – two qualifying language papers (Odia and English) in Part-I and seven papers in Part-II (Essay, General Studies-I, II, III, IV and two Optional subject papers).
  • Marks obtained in Part-II papers and Interview (Personality Test) are counted for ranking; language papers in Part-I are qualifying in nature.
  • Interview (Personality Test) carries 250 marks; final ranking is based on total marks of Main Written and Interview.
  • Candidates are allotted to various Services based on ranks and service preference.

General Information/Instructions

  • The provisions of the Odisha Conduct of Examinations Act, 1988 are applicable; any violation or malpractice will attract disciplinary action and possible criminal prosecution.
  • Penalty provisions under Rule-18 of Odisha Civil Services Combined Competitive Recruitment Examination Rules, 1991 shall apply.
  • Reservation and relaxation benefits for SC, ST and SEBC are admissible only to those categories of Odisha.
  • Community/caste status once mentioned in the online application shall be treated as final and cannot be changed later.
  • The advertisement does not bind the Government to make appointment; the number of vacancies is subject to change without notice depending on public service requirements.
  • Misrepresentation or suppression of information in the online application will result in cancellation of candidature and penalty as decided by the Commission.
  • Mere empanelment in the select list does not confer any right to appointment unless the Government is satisfied about suitability after necessary enquiry.
  • No request for withdrawal of candidature or change of category will be entertained.
  • Candidates must carefully fill service/post preference; change of preference after submission of online application will not be allowed.
  • Candidates must answer papers in their own handwriting; only PwD candidates with specified disabilities may use a scribe as per rules.

How to Apply

  • Candidates must go through the detailed advertisement available on the website of OPSC before filling the Online Application Form.
  • Candidates must apply online through the OPSC website (https://opsc.gov.in).
  • The link for registration and payment of examination fee will be available from 20/01/2026 to 20/02/2026 (5.00 P.M.).
  • The last date for submission of registered online application is 27/02/2026 (5.00 P.M.).
  • Applications received through any mode other than online shall not be accepted and will be summarily rejected.
  • After declaration of result of the Main Written Examination, candidates called for Interview/Personality Test will be required to submit print-out/hard copy of online application along with photocopies of documents as stated in the advertisement on the day of document verification.

UPSC CSE 2026 – Preliminary Examination Pattern

The Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination is the first stage of the UPSC selection process. It is a screening test used to shortlist candidates for the Main Examination. Marks scored in Prelims are not counted in the final merit ranking.

Paper Subject Type Marks Duration
Paper I General Studies (GS) Objective (MCQs) 200 Marks 2 Hours
Paper II CSAT (Aptitude Test) Objective (MCQs) 200 Marks 2 Hours

Prelims Key Rules

  • Both papers are objective type (Multiple Choice Questions).
  • Paper II (CSAT) is qualifying in nature – minimum 33% marks required.
  • Marks of Paper I are considered for cutoff and shortlisting for Mains.
  • Negative marking applies: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
  • Leaving a question blank carries no penalty.

UPSC CSE 2026 – Main Examination Pattern

The Civil Services (Main) Examination is the second stage and consists of a written examination followed by an Interview/Personality Test. Marks obtained in the written papers and interview are counted for the final merit list.

Paper Subject Marks Nature
Paper A Compulsory Indian Language 300 Qualifying
Paper B English 300 Qualifying
Paper I Essay 250 Merit
Paper II General Studies I 250 Merit
Paper III General Studies II 250 Merit
Paper IV General Studies III 250 Merit
Paper V General Studies IV (Ethics) 250 Merit
Paper VI Optional Subject – Paper 1 250 Merit
Paper VII Optional Subject – Paper 2 250 Merit

Main Exam Structure

  • Total Written Papers: 9
  • Qualifying Papers: 2 (Indian Language & English)
  • Merit Papers: 7
  • Total Marks (Written): 1750

Interview / Personality Test

Stage Marks
Personality Test / Interview 275

Final Merit Calculation

  • Written Exam Marks: 1750
  • Interview Marks: 275
  • Total Merit Marks: 2025

Important Notes

  • Prelims marks are used only for qualification, not for final ranking.
  • Mains + Interview marks decide final service allocation.
  • Negative marking applies in Prelims only.
  • Candidates must qualify in both language papers to have their merit papers evaluated.

Selection Process for RRB Group D CEN 09/2025

The recruitment consists of 4 successive stages:

Stage 1: Computer Based Test (CBT)

Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for candidates using scribe)

Total Questions: 100 (Each of 1 mark)

Subject Number of Questions
General Science 25
Mathematics 25
General Intelligence and Reasoning 30
General Awareness and Current Affairs 20
TOTAL 100 Questions = 100 Marks

Exam Pattern:

  • Objective type with multiple choices
  • Questions available in English, Hindi, and 13 regional languages (Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu)
  • Negative Marking: 1/3 mark deducted for each wrong answer
  • Section-wise distribution may vary slightly in actual exam

Minimum Qualifying Marks:

  • UR: 40%
  • EWS: 40%
  • OBC-NCL: 30%
  • SC: 30%
  • ST: 30%
  • PwBD: May be relaxed by 2 marks in case of shortage

Syllabus (Indicative):

  • Mathematics: Number system, BODMAS, Decimals, Fractions, LCM, HCF, Ratio & Proportion, Percentages, Mensuration, Time & Work, Time & Distance, Simple & Compound Interest, Profit & Loss, Algebra, Geometry, Trigonometry, Elementary Statistics, Square root, Age Calculations, Calendar & Clock, Pipes & Cistern
  • General Intelligence & Reasoning: Analogies, Alphabetical & Number Series, Coding & Decoding, Mathematical operations, Relationships, Syllogism, Jumbling, Venn Diagram, Data Interpretation & Sufficiency, Conclusions & Decision making, Similarities & Differences, Analytical Reasoning, Classification, Directions, Statement-Arguments & Assumptions
  • General Science: Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences of 10th standard level (CBSE)
  • General Awareness & Current Affairs: Science & Technology, Sports, Culture, Personalities, Economics, Politics, and other important subjects

Normalization: Marks will be normalized if CBT conducted in multiple sessions

Stage 2: Physical Efficiency Test (PET)

Shortlisting: 3 times the total vacancies (may vary) based on CBT merit

Nature: Qualifying (Mandatory to pass - marks not counted for final merit)

Candidate Type Test 1: Weight Carrying Test 2: Running
Male Candidates Lift and carry 35 kg weight for 100 meters in 2 minutes (in one chance, without putting down) Run 1000 meters in 4 minutes 15 seconds (in one chance)
Female Candidates Lift and carry 20 kg weight for 100 meters in 2 minutes (in one chance, without putting down) Run 1000 meters in 5 minutes 40 seconds (in one chance)
Transgender Candidates Same relaxed standards as Female candidates

Important PET Notes:

  • Two-stage test: First weight carrying, then running (after recovery gap)
  • Failing in weight carrying means elimination (no running test)
  • Weight carrying involves lifting sandbag (without handle) from waist-height bench and carrying without dropping
  • Candidates' responsibility to ensure medical fitness for PET - Railways not responsible for injuries
  • Exemptions from PET:
    • Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) - must pass medical examination
    • Course Completed Act Apprentices (CCAA)
    • Ex-Servicemen (ExSM)
  • Pregnant Candidates: Must submit self-declaration. If pregnant, PET deferred till 6 weeks post-confinement. Vacancy kept reserved.

Stage 3: Document Verification (DV)

  • Shortlisting: 1:1 ratio of vacancies based on CBT merit + PET qualification
  • Candidates must produce original certificates
  • No additional time given - absence leads to candidature cancellation
  • Scanned copies to be uploaded before DV at https://oirms-ir.gov.in/rrbdv
  • Certificates must be in English/Hindi (translated version required otherwise)
  • Hard copy of signed application form to be brought

Stage 4: Medical Examination (ME)

  • Conducted by Railway Medical Authorities
  • Must pass requisite medical fitness test as per IRMM
  • Visual acuity standards strictly enforced
  • Medical appeal option available (one final opportunity on payment)
  • Candidates found medically unsuitable will NOT be given alternative appointment

Final Merit & Selection

  • Based on CBT marks (after normalization if applicable)
  • Subject to PET qualification, DV clearance, and medical fitness
  • Post/Railway allotment as per candidate's preference, merit, medical fitness, and vacancy
  • In case of tie: Older candidate ranked higher; if age also same, alphabetical order of name (A to Z)
  • No right to appointment - RRB/RRC only recommends; appointment by Railway Administration

Eligibility Criteria

  • Nationality:
    • A candidate must be a citizen of India
    • With the consent of the Central Government signified in writing, subjects of Nepal or Bhutan may also be appointed
  • Sex: Both Male and Female candidates are eligible for appointment to the post of Assistant Commandants
  • Educational Qualification:
    • A candidate must hold a Bachelor's degree of a University incorporated by an Act of the Central or State Legislature in India
    • OR from educational institutions established by an Act of Parliament
    • OR declared to be deemed as a University under Section-3 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956
    • OR possess an equivalent qualification
    • Candidates who have appeared at an examination the passing of which would render them educationally qualified but have not been informed of the results will also be eligible
    • Candidates who intend to appear at such a qualifying examination in the year 2026 will also be eligible
    • However, qualified candidates must produce proof of passing the requisite qualifying examination (Degree Certificate/Final Mark Sheet/Provisional Degree Certificate) within the time limit prescribed in the Rules
    • Degree/Post Graduate/Diploma qualifications acquired through distance learning/part-time are NOT considered
  • Important Notes:
    • In exceptional cases, the Commission may treat a candidate who does not have the foregoing qualifications as qualified, provided the candidate has passed an examination of equivalent standard
    • Candidates possessing professional and technical qualifications recognized by Government as equivalent to professional and technical degrees are also eligible
    • All qualifications must be from UGC-recognised Universities/Deemed Universities/MHRD-approved autonomous institutions

Salary/Stipend

  • Post: Assistant Commandants (Group A) in Central Armed Police Forces
  • Pay Scale: Details not mentioned in the notification
  • Candidates will receive salary and allowances as per Government of India rules applicable to Group A officers in Central Armed Police Forces
  • The selected candidates will be appointed in BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP, or SSB based on their merit rank and force preference

Age Limit (as on 01-08-2026)

  • Minimum Age: 20 years (must have been born not later than 1st August, 2006)
  • Maximum Age: 25 years (must have been born not earlier than 2nd August, 2001)
  • Age Relaxation:
    • SC/ST candidates: Up to a maximum of 5 years
    • OBC candidates: Up to a maximum of 3 years (for those eligible to avail reservation)
    • Civilian Central Government Servants/Ex-Servicemen: Up to a maximum of 5 years in accordance with existing Central Government instructions (total relaxation limited to 5 years)
    • SC/ST and OBC candidates who are also Civilian Central Government Servants/Ex-servicemen: Eligible for cumulative age-relaxation under both categories
  • Important Notes on Age:
    • The date of birth accepted is that entered in the Matriculation or Secondary School Leaving Certificate or equivalent certificate
    • No other document relating to age (Horoscopes, Affidavits, Birth extracts from Municipal Corporation, Service records) will be accepted
    • Once Date of Birth has been submitted in the Online Application Form, no change will be allowed subsequently on any grounds whatsoever
    • Save as provided above, the age limits prescribed can in no case be relaxed

  • Payment of fee through any other mode is neither valid nor acceptable

Written Exam Timing - Paper-II 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM
e-Admit Card Download Date Last working day of preceding week of examination date
Physical Standards Tests / Physical Efficiency Tests After declaration of Written Exam result
Interview / Personality Test After PST/PET (for qualified candidates)
Medical Standards Tests After Interview / Personality Test

Selection Process

  • Stage 1: Written Examination (19th July, 2026)
    • Paper-I: General Ability and Intelligence - 250 Marks
      • Duration: 2 hours (10:00 AM to 12:00 Noon)
      • Type: Objective (Multiple Choice) Type questions
      • Medium: English as well as Hindi
      • Subjects: General Mental Ability (logical reasoning, quantitative aptitude, numerical ability, data interpretation), General Science, Current Events of National & International Importance, Indian Polity & Economy, History of India, Indian & World Geography
      • There will be penalty (Negative Marking) for wrong answers: One third (0.33) of the marks assigned to a question will be deducted for each wrong answer
    • Paper-II: General Studies, Essay and Comprehension - 200 Marks
      • Duration: 3 hours (2:00 PM to 5:00 PM)
      • Type: Conventional (Descriptive) Type
      • Part-A: Essay questions (80 Marks) - to be answered in long narrative form either in Hindi or English. Topics: modern Indian history especially freedom struggle, geography, polity and economy, security and human rights issues, analytical ability
      • Part-B: Comprehension, précis writing, other communications/language skills (120 Marks) - to be attempted in English only. Topics: Comprehension passages, précis writing, developing counter arguments, simple grammar and other language testing aspects
      • Candidates must write answers only in the medium allowed. No credit for answers written in other medium
    • There will be minimum qualifying marks separately in each Paper as may be fixed by the Commission
    • Paper-I will be evaluated first and Paper-II will be evaluated only for those who obtain minimum qualifying marks in Paper-I
  • Stage 2: Physical Standards Tests (PST) / Physical Efficiency Tests (PET)
    • Conducted for candidates qualified in Written Examination
    • Physical Standards Requirements:
      • Men: Height 165 cm, Chest 81 cm (unexpanded) with 5 cm minimum expansion, Weight 50 kg
      • Women: Height 157 cm, Weight 46 kg
      • Height and chest measurement will be measured correct to one decimal in centimeter
      • Weight should be as per height and age as per prescribed chart
    • Physical Efficiency Tests:
      • Men: 100 Meter Race in 16 Seconds, 800 Meter Race in 3 Min 45 Sec, Long Jump 3.5 Meters (3 Chances), Shot Put (7.26 Kg) 4.5 Meters (3 Chances)
      • Women: 100 Meter Race in 18 Seconds, 800 Meter Race in 4 Min 45 Sec, Long Jump 3.0 Meters (3 Chances)
    • Female candidates must submit self-declaration about pregnancy status before PST/PET
    • Conducted under supervision of Nodal Authority appointed by Ministry of Home Affairs
  • Stage 3: Interview / Personality Test
    • Only for candidates qualified in PST/PET
    • Marks: 150 Marks
    • Conducted by Union Public Service Commission
    • Candidates declared unqualified in PET will not be called for Interview
    • NCC 'B' or 'C' Certificate holders will be given consideration at Interview stage
  • Stage 4: Medical Standards Tests (MST)
    • Conducted only for candidates who appeared in Interview/Personality Test
    • Detailed Medical Standards prescribed for Eye Sight, Ear, Nose, Neck, Teeth, General Health, etc.
    • Eye Sight: Better eye 6/6 or 6/9 (corrected), Worse eye 6/12 or 6/9 (corrected), Near Vision N6/N9 (corrected), Colour Perception CP-III by ISIHARA plates
    • LASIK surgery correction permitted subject to prescribed criteria
    • Candidates declared 'UNFIT' can appear before Review Medical Board preferably next day of DME
    • Appeals against MST results must be made within 24 hours after declaration of DME results
    • Conducted under supervision of Nodal Authority appointed by Ministry of Home Affairs
  • Final Selection/Merit:
    • Merit list drawn on basis of marks obtained in Written Examination and Interview/Personality Test
    • Any candidate found not satisfying prescribed Medical Standards after MST will not be appointed
    • Tie Breaking Principle: (i) Higher marks in written total, (ii) Higher marks in Paper-I, (iii) Senior in age, (iv) At Commission's discretion

How to Apply

  • Candidates are required to apply online only using the Commission's website: https://upsconline.nic.in
  • No other mode is allowed for submission of application
  • Application Process has Four Modules:
    • Module 1: Account Creation - Can be filled anytime (common for all exams)
    • Module 2: Universal Registration (URN) - Can be filled anytime (common for all exams). URN generated is unique and remains constant for all UPSC exams
    • Module 3: Common Application Form (CAF) - Can be filled anytime (common for all exams)
    • Module 4: Examination Specific Module - Can be filled only during notification period (includes fees, centres, force preferences, etc.)
  • Documents Required:
    • Recent passport-size colour photograph (scanned in .jpg format, 20 KB to 200 KB)
    • Signature (scanned - sign three times one below other on plain white paper using black ink, .jpg format, 20 KB to 100 KB)
    • Live photograph (to be captured while filling CAF)
    • One Photo ID Card details (Aadhaar/Voter/PAN/Passport/Driving License/Any other Government Photo ID)
    • Date of Birth certificate (Matriculation/Secondary School Leaving Certificate)
    • Educational qualification certificates and mark sheets
    • Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS) in prescribed format, if applicable
    • OBC candidates: OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate based on income for FY 2024-25, 2023-24, 2022-23, issued on/after 01.04.2025 but not later than 12.03.2026
    • EWS candidates: EWS Certificate based on income for FY 2024-25, issued on/after 01.04.2025 but not later than 12.03.2026
    • Ex-servicemen: Prescribed Certificate and Undertaking as per Appendix-VI(A) and VI(B)
  • Read General Instructions, Profile/Module-wise Instructions, and Instructions for uploading documents carefully before filling the form
  • Prepare requisite documents in advance for smooth flow during form filling
  • Pay application fee (if applicable) through Net Banking/Credit/Debit Card/UPI
  • Select examination centre from available options (first-apply-first-allot basis)
  • Indicate force preferences (BSF/CRPF/CISF/ITBP/SSB)
  • Review all entered information carefully before final submission
  • Take printout or save soft copy of submitted application for future reference
  • Last Date: 12th March, 2026 (till 18:00 hours)
  • Candidates are strongly advised to apply online well in time without waiting for the last date
  • After Written Exam Result: Qualified candidates must login within 15 days window and update details/educational qualification status with proof, failing which will not be allowed in further stages
  • Download e-Admit Card from Commission's website on last working day of preceding week of examination
  • No Admit Card will be sent by post or email

Odisha Sub-ordinate Staff Selection Commission (OSSSC) RI, ARI and ICDS Supervisor and Other Notification 2026 has been released on 07-01-2026 on the official website https://osssc.gov.in. A total of 3,250 vacancies have been announced through the OSSSC Recruitment 2026 (Advt No. IIE-120/2025-3219/OSSSC).

Candidates aged 20 to 42 years (with applicable relaxations as per rules) who possess the required Post-wise educational qualifications and other eligibility conditions as prescribed in the Detailed Advertisement for CRE-2025 are eligible to apply for these vacancies.

The online application process for OSSSC RI, ARI and ICDS Supervisor and Other Recruitment 2026 has started on 07-01-2026 and will remain open until 06-03-2026 (including fee payment). Candidates can download the official notification PDF and apply online through the direct links provided below in this article.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Revenue Inspector (RI): Bachelor’s Degree in any discipline or equivalent from a recognized University with knowledge in computer application. Age: over 20 years and below 42 years as on 1st January, 2025.
  • ICDS Supervisor: Bachelor’s Degree in Arts, Science or Commerce or its equivalent. Only women candidates; age not less than 21 years and not more than 42 years as on 1st January, 2025.
  • Village Agricultural Worker (VAW): Passed +2 Science or +2 Vocational course in Agriculture related subject in Crop Production (CP) / Horticulture (HORT) / Repair and Maintenance of Power Driven Farm Machinery (PDFM) from a recognized Board/Council/Institution; Diploma in Agriculture Polytechnic under OUAT is desirable and carries 5% extra marks in Written Test.
  • Junior Assistant (JA): Passed +3 in Arts / Science / Commerce or equivalent with knowledge of Computer Skill.
  • Assistant Revenue Inspector (ARI): Passed Higher Secondary Examination (10+2) conducted by CHSE, Odisha or equivalent, or Diploma in Engineering from Institution under State Council for Technical Education & Vocational Training, Odisha affiliated to AICTE, having knowledge in computer application.
  • Amin: Passed Higher Secondary Examination (10+2) conducted by CHSE, Odisha or equivalent, or Diploma in Engineering from Institution under State Council for Technical Education & Vocational Training, Odisha affiliated to AICTE, with knowledge in computer application (as per detailed table text).
  • Statistical Field Surveyor (SFS): Passed 10+2 examination conducted by CHSE, Odisha or CBSE or CISCE or any other examination equivalent thereto.
  • Odia language: Must be able to read, write and speak Odia and must have passed ME School Exam with Odia as language subject, or Matriculation with Odia as medium in non-language subjects, or passed Odia as a language subject in Class VII or above, or passed Odia language test in ME School Standard conducted by School & Mass Education Department.
  • Other criteria: Must be a citizen of India, of good character, and if married must not have more than one spouse living except as exempted under personal law.
  • Junior Assistant-specific: Must have registered name in an Employment Exchange of the concerned district (or State/Special Employment Exchange with Resident Certificate of concerned district) on or before the date of submission of online application.
  • Persons with Disabilities (PwDs): Must possess Permanent Disability Certificate / UDID card with not less than 40% disability in the category and sub-category suitable for the post, as per Annexures I to VII.
  • Ex-Servicemen: Must possess Identity Card/Discharge Certificate/documents in support of defence service and furnish an undertaking about non-availment of earlier re-employment under Government of Odisha.

Salary/Stipend

  • Revenue Inspector (RI): Pay Scale ₹ 35400–112400, Pay Matrix Level-9, Cell-01 under R & DM Department.
  • ICDS Supervisor: Pay Scale ₹ 35400–112400, Pay Matrix Level-9, Cell-01 under W & CD Department.
  • Village Agricultural Worker (VAW): Pay Scale ₹ 21700–69100, Pay Matrix Level-5, Cell-01 under A & FE Department.
  • Junior Assistant (JA): Pay Scale ₹ 19900–63200, Pay Matrix Level-4, Cell-01 under Finance, R & DM, A & FE, W & CD Departments.
  • Assistant Revenue Inspector (ARI): Pay Scale ₹ 19900–63200, Pay Matrix Level-4, Cell-01 under R & DM Department.
  • Amin: Pay Scale ₹ 18000–56900, Pay Matrix Level-3, Cell-01 under R & DM Department.
  • Statistical Field Surveyor (SFS): Pay Scale ₹ 18000–56900, Pay Matrix Level-3, Cell-01 under Planning & Convergence Department.

Age Limit

  • Revenue Inspector (RI): Over 20 years and below 42 years.
  • ICDS Supervisor: Not less than 21 years and not more than 42 years; Anganwadi Workers get additional 5 years relaxation for ICDS Supervisor only, besides general relaxation.
  • Village Agricultural Worker (VAW): Minimum 21 years and maximum 42 years.
  • Junior Assistant (JA): Minimum 21 years and maximum 42 years.
  • Assistant Revenue Inspector (ARI): Over 20 years and below 42 years.
  • Amin: As per post-wise age and educational qualification table, within 21–42 years.
  • Statistical Field Surveyor (SFS): Minimum 21 years and maximum 42 years.
  • SC/ST/SEBC: Upper age relaxed by 5 years.
  • Women (for RI, ARI, VAW, JA, Amin & SFS): Upper age relaxed by 5 years; for ICDS Supervisor (women-only post) this additional 5 years is not applicable, except for Anganwadi Workers as stated.
  • Persons with Disabilities (PwDs): Upper age relaxed by 10 years; PwDs of SC/ST/SEBC entitled to cumulative age relaxation over category relaxation as per Odisha Civil Service (Fixation of Upper Age Limit) Rules, 1989.
  • Ex-Servicemen: For RI & ICDS Supervisor, upper age relaxed by 5 years; for other posts, relaxation by total period of defence service rendered, subject to conditions mentioned.
  • RI, ARI & Amin: Age relaxation up to five years for candidates having actual work experience in settlement/consolidation organisations.

Application Fee

  • As per Odisha Payment of Recruitment Examination Fees and Refund Rules, 2025.
  • Candidates other than Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST) and Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) shall pay Examination Fee of ₹ 500/- using Net Banking / Credit Card / Debit Card / UPI through Payment Gateway during online application.
  • SC, ST and PwDs candidates are exempted from payment of Examination Fee.
  • Examination fee of ₹ 500/- shall be refunded to applicants who actually appear in the examination, after verification of attendance records, to the same bank account / payment method used at registration.
  • No refund is admissible to applicants who fail to appear in the examination for any reason.
  • If Confirmation Page is not generated after fee payment, transaction will be cancelled and refund credited within 48 hours; applicant must make another payment for successful application in such cases.

Important Dates

Event Start Date End Date
Online Registration (Fresh candidates – New User who have not registered earlier) 07.01.2026 31.01.2026
Re-registration (Registered User who already have User ID for any previous post) 07.01.2026 31.01.2026

Selection Process

  • Stage-I: Written Test – 100 marks, MCQ type in OMR/CBRE mode, of minimum standard of High School Certificate Examination.
  • Written Test pattern: Mathematics (20 questions, 20 marks), General Studies (20, 20), English (20, 20), Odia (15, 15), Computer (15, 15), Logical Reasoning (10, 10); duration 1½ hours.
  • Negative marking: One-fourth (0.25) of marks assigned to a question deducted for each wrong answer; multiple answers treated as wrong; no penalty for unattempted questions.
  • Minimum qualifying marks (Written): 30% for ST, SC, PwDs, Ex-Servicemen and Sportspersons; 35% for others. VAW candidates with Diploma in Agriculture Polytechnic (OUAT) get 5% extra marks (capped at total marks).
  • Stage-II: Practical Skill Test in Basic Computer Skills – 50 marks, 1 hour; qualifying in nature with minimum 40% for all candidates.
  • Number of candidates shortlisted for Practical Skill Test: not less than 3 times the number of vacancies, category/special category wise, as per merit and availability; Commission may vary as per requirement.
  • Merit Lists: Provisional Master Merit List based on marks / normalized score in Written Test; Provisional Screening List for Practical Skill Test; Provisional Merit List of Practical Skill Test; Screening List for Document Verification; Provisional Select Lists post-wise / district-wise.
  • Document Verification & Counselling: Shortlisted candidates undergo document verification by District Level Board and then counselling for choice of post and Department/District/Range; allotment based on merit-cum-choice and availability.
  • Commission reserves right to conduct additional/re-test for Written/Skill Test, reschedule tests, and cancel part or whole of recruitment at any stage.

General Information/Instructions

  • Candidates must apply online only through OSSSC website; applications other than online / incomplete shall be summarily rejected.
  • All eligibility conditions (except age) must be fulfilled as on the last date of submission of online application.
  • No Admission Letter shall be issued to candidates whose application is incomplete or who do not fulfil prescribed eligibility criteria.
  • Provisional Admission Letters / Intimation Letters for Written Test and Practical Skill Test shall be uploaded on www.osssc.gov.in only; no hard copy will be sent by post.
  • Candidates must regularly visit the Commission’s website to track notices, exam dates, and download Admission / Intimation Letters using User ID and Password.
  • Information uploaded on website will not be supplied separately under RTI Act, 2005 and will remain available for a specific period only; candidates should download and preserve it.
  • Candidature remains purely provisional and is liable to rejection at any stage for deficiency / misrepresentation / use of unfair means.
  • Multiple application forms by a candidate are not permitted and will lead to cancellation of result and other penalties as per rules.
  • In CBRE mode, appearing in more than one shift/date by furnishing false information is treated as unfair means and penalised.
  • Commission’s decision on eligibility, acceptance/rejection of applications, penalties, mode of selection, exam conduct, test centre allotment, preparation of merit list, allocation of post, and debarment is final and binding.

How to Apply

  • Visit OSSSC website www.osssc.gov.in and click on “Apply Online”.
  • Registration (New User): Fresh candidates who have not registered earlier for any recruitment of OSSSC must complete Registration by providing required details and uploading full specimen signature and passport-size photograph in prescribed formats and sizes.
  • Re-registration (Registered User): Candidates already registered for any other OSSSC post must login using existing User ID and select “Re-registration” option for this post.
  • Mere Registration / Re-registration does not mean filing of online application; candidates must login again and fill and submit the detailed Online Application Form as per instructions on the screen.
  • Fill in all data and information as per certificates/records, upload required documents, and make Examination Fee payment (if applicable) through available online payment modes.
  • Ensure that the photograph and signature uploaded are clearly identifiable/visible; otherwise registration/application is liable to rejection.
  • Use own valid personal e-mail ID and mobile number with validity till completion of recruitment process for receiving Activation Key, alerts, and for downloading Admission Letters; do not share or change this contact during the process.
  • Submit online application well in advance without waiting for the last date to avoid last-hour rush.
  • Take printout of Confirmation Page after successful submission and fee payment (where applicable).

UPSC CSE 2026 – Preliminary Examination Pattern

The Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination is the first stage of the UPSC selection process. It is a screening test used to shortlist candidates for the Main Examination. Marks scored in Prelims are not counted in the final merit ranking.

Paper Subject Type Marks Duration
Paper I General Studies (GS) Objective (MCQs) 200 Marks 2 Hours
Paper II CSAT (Aptitude Test) Objective (MCQs) 200 Marks 2 Hours

Prelims Key Rules

  • Both papers are objective type (Multiple Choice Questions).
  • Paper II (CSAT) is qualifying in nature – minimum 33% marks required.
  • Marks of Paper I are considered for cutoff and shortlisting for Mains.
  • Negative marking applies: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
  • Leaving a question blank carries no penalty.

UPSC CSE 2026 – Main Examination Pattern

The Civil Services (Main) Examination is the second stage and consists of a written examination followed by an Interview/Personality Test. Marks obtained in the written papers and interview are counted for the final merit list.

Paper Subject Marks Nature
Paper A Compulsory Indian Language 300 Qualifying
Paper B English 300 Qualifying
Paper I Essay 250 Merit
Paper II General Studies I 250 Merit
Paper III General Studies II 250 Merit
Paper IV General Studies III 250 Merit
Paper V General Studies IV (Ethics) 250 Merit
Paper VI Optional Subject – Paper 1 250 Merit
Paper VII Optional Subject – Paper 2 250 Merit

Main Exam Structure

  • Total Written Papers: 9
  • Qualifying Papers: 2 (Indian Language & English)
  • Merit Papers: 7
  • Total Marks (Written): 1750

Interview / Personality Test

Stage Marks
Personality Test / Interview 275

Final Merit Calculation

  • Written Exam Marks: 1750
  • Interview Marks: 275
  • Total Merit Marks: 2025

Important Notes

  • Prelims marks are used only for qualification, not for final ranking.
  • Mains + Interview marks decide final service allocation.
  • Negative marking applies in Prelims only.
  • Candidates must qualify in both language papers to have their merit papers evaluated.

Eligibility Criteria

Qualifications

  • Professor - Eligibility (A or B):
    • Option A: An eminent scholar having a Ph.D. degree in the concerned/allied/relevant discipline, and published work of high quality, actively engaged in research with evidence of published work with a minimum of 10 research publications in the peer-reviewed or UGC-listed journals and a total research score of 120 as per UGC Regulations-2018. A minimum of ten years of teaching experience in university/college as Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor, and/or research experience at equivalent level at the University/National Level Institutions with evidence of having successfully guided doctoral candidate
    • Option B: An outstanding professional, having a Ph.D. degree in the relevant/allied/applied disciplines, from any academic institutions/industry, who has made significant contribution to the knowledge in the concerned/allied/relevant discipline, supported by documentary evidence provided he/she has ten years experience
  • Associate Professor: A good academic record, with a Ph.D. Degree in the concerned/allied/relevant disciplines. A Master's Degree with at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade in a point-scale, wherever the grading system is followed). A minimum of eight years of experience of teaching and/or research in an academic/research position equivalent to that of Assistant Professor in a University, College or Accredited Research Institution/industry with a minimum of seven publications in the peer-reviewed or UGC-listed journals and a total research score of Seventy five (75) as per UGC Regulations-2018
  • Assistant Professor - Eligibility (A or B):
    • Option A: A Master's degree with 55% marks (or an equivalent grade in a point-scale wherever the grading system is followed) in a concerned/relevant/allied subject from an Indian University, or an equivalent degree from an accredited foreign university. Besides fulfilling the above qualifications, the candidate must have cleared the National Eligibility Test (NET) conducted by the UGC or the CSIR, or a similar test accredited by the UGC, like SLET/SET or who are or have been awarded a Ph.D. Degree in accordance with the University Grants Commission Regulations, 2009 or 2016 and their amendments from time to time as the case may be exempted from NET/SLET/SET
    • Option B: The Ph.D degree has been obtained from a foreign university/institution with a ranking among top 500 in the World University Ranking (at any time) by any one of the following: (i) Quacquarelli Symonds (QS) (ii) the Times Higher Education (THE) or (iii) the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) of the Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Shanghai)
  • Deputy Librarian: A Master's Degree in library science/information science/documentation science, with at least 55% marks or an equivalent grade in a point-scale, wherever grading system is followed. Eight years experience as an Assistant University Librarian/College Librarian. Evidence of innovative library services including integration of ICT in library. A Ph.D. Degree in library science/Information science/Documentation Science/Archives and manuscript keeping/computerization of library
  • Assistant Librarian: A Master's Degree in Library Science, Information Science or Documentation Science or an equivalent professional degree, with at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade in a point-scale, wherever the grading system is followed). A consistently good academic record, with knowledge of computerization of a library. Besides fulfilling the above qualifications, the candidate must have cleared the National Eligibility Test (NET) conducted by the UGC, CSIR or similar test accredited by the UGC like SLET/SET or who are or have been awarded a Ph.D. Degree in accordance with the University Grants Commission Regulations, 2009 or 2016 and their amendments from time to time

Eligibility Criteria – Telangana High Court Office Subordinate Recruitment 2026

Educational Qualification

  • Candidate must have passed any examination between 7th to 10th class or its equivalent.
  • Candidates having qualification higher than 10th class are not eligible.
  • Applicants must mention any work experience such as cooking, carpentry, plumbing, electrical, painting, etc., as relevant to duties at residences of Judicial Officers.
  • Educational qualification must be possessed as on the date of notification (02.02.2026).

Age Limit (as on 01-07-2026)

  • Minimum age: 18 years.
  • Maximum age: 46 years.

Age Relaxation (as per Telangana State & Subordinate Service Rules)

  • SC / ST / BC / EWS: 5 years.
  • Persons with Disabilities (PWD): 10 years.
  • For candidates working on contract or outsourcing basis in specified judicial/legal services – relaxation as per rules, provided they were within age limit at initial appointment and have at least 2 years of service by date of notification.

Reservation

  • Reservation applicable for SC, ST, BC, EWS, Persons with Disability (40% and above), and Women, as per Government of Telangana orders.
  • Community must be recognized as BC/SC/ST in the State of Telangana as per G.O.Ms references; otherwise, candidate is treated as Open Category.
  • 33 1/3% horizontal reservation for Women will be implemented.
  • Reservation for EWS will be as per relevant G.O.Ms issued by Government of Telangana.

Selection Process – Telangana High Court Office Subordinate 2026

OMR Based Examination & Viva-Voce

  • OMR-based written examination (objective type, multiple choice) – 45 marks.
  • Oral interview (Viva-voce) – 5 marks.
  • Question paper: General Knowledge, 45 questions, 1 mark each, duration 60 minutes.
  • Question paper will be in two languages – English and Telugu.

Minimum Qualifying Marks

  • OC & EWS: 45% in OMR examination.
  • BC: 40% in OMR examination.
  • SC / ST / PH: 35% in OMR examination.

Shortlisting & Weightage

  • Candidates qualified in OMR exam will be shortlisted in 1:3 ratio of notified/available vacancies for certificate verification and viva-voce.
  • Weightage marks will be given to candidates working on contract/outsourcing basis in notified judicial/legal services based on length of service, subject to minimum 2 years of service and securing minimum qualifying marks.

Merit List

  • Merit list will be prepared on the basis of marks secured in OMR examination and viva-voce.
  • In case of tie in total marks, elder candidate in age will be preferred.
  • If tie persists, candidate with higher marks in prescribed educational qualification will be considered.

Application / Examination Fee

  • OC & BC candidates: Rs. 600/- (excluding service charges).
  • SC / ST / EWS / PWD candidates: Rs. 400/- (excluding service charges).
  • Concessional fee of Rs. 400/- for SC/ST is applicable only to communities recognized as SC/ST in Telangana.
  • Fee must be paid online only; once paid, it is non-refundable under any circumstances.

How to Apply Online for Telangana High Court Office Subordinate Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official website of the High Court for the State of Telangana: https://tshc.gov.in.
  2. Click on the recruitment/notifications section and open the link for “Notification No. 101/2026 – Office Subordinate Recruitment”.
  3. Complete Part-A: One Time Profile Registration (OTPR) by entering your basic details to generate OTPR ID and password.
  4. Login using the OTPR ID and password and proceed to Part-B: Application Form for Office Subordinate posts.
  5. Fill in all required details carefully – personal details, educational qualification (7th to 10th class), community, disability (if any), and work experience (cooking, carpentry, plumbing, electrical, painting, etc.).
  6. Upload scanned copies of required certificates/documents in PDF format (as per instructions in the user guide) and recent passport-size photograph and signature, if required.
  7. Pay the applicable online application/examination fee as per your category through the available online payment modes.
  8. Submit the online application and take a printout / save the application and payment receipt for future reference.

Important: Candidates must keep all scanned certificates ready in PDF format before starting the online application. Particulars furnished in the online form will be treated as final, and any wrong information regarding category/caste may forfeit the claim for reservation.

Application Fee

  • The applicants have to pay an amount of Rs.500/- (Rupees five hundred only)
  • The said examination fee has to be paid by way of a crossed Demand Draft drawn in favour of "THE REGISTRAR (RECRUITMENT), HIGH COURT FOR THE STATE OF TELANGANA", payable at Hyderabad

Important Dates
